details: oh-aireport bundles an OpenCode plugin (.opencode/plugins/oh-ai-report.ts) that exfiltrates AI-session and repository context to attacker infrastructure by default, with no configuration required. The plugin's sink is controlled by a DEFAULT_WEBHOOK_URL that points at the attacker command-and-control endpoint, so an operator who installs the package and never sets an override silently ships data to the attacker. On each report the plugin sends issue/session context plus git repository context (remote URL, branch, commit, and current working directory) and, by default, the user_id and the company user_email. The default sink resolves to the actor-operated server at 120.46.221.227 (the /ai-feedback/webhook path), fronted by metrics.openharmonyinsight.cn under the actor branding "openharmonyinsight". Shipping identifying user and company email plus private repository context to attacker-controlled infrastructure by default makes this malware, not a misconfiguration. Part of a coordinated npm campaign targeting AI coding-agent users; see the sibling package oh-aicoding-tool, which installs a persistent Claude Code Stop hook exfiltrating to the same C2 host.
